gdp_growth.label: GDP growth (QoQ)
gdp_growth.note: Growth has stabilised as the 2022 energy-price shock fades, but the ECB flags the Middle East war, trade friction and Russia's war against Ukraine as the main downside risks to the outlook via weaker investment, exports and consumption.

cpi.label: CPI (HICP, YoY)
cpi.note: Disinflation continues toward the 2% target. ECB sees upside risk if energy prices rise further and spill over into wages and other prices, or if trade tensions fragment supply chains and constrain raw materials.

interest_rates.label: ECB main refinancing rate
interest_rates.note: ECB rate path has been on an easing trend since the 2023-24 peak as inflation cooled; further moves stay data-dependent given the geopolitical risk premium the ECB continues to flag.

energy_prices.label: Energy prices (TTF gas)
energy_prices.note: TTF remains structurally above pre-2022 levels. ECB warns a prolonged escalation could disrupt energy supply further; shipping continues to be rerouted via the Cape of Good Hope due to Red Sea/Suez security risks.

currency.label: EUR/USD
currency.note: EUR/USD driven mainly by the relative ECB/Fed policy stance and safe-haven flows; the ECB's own bulletins don't target FX directly but note geopolitical risk as a source of volatility across asset markets.

manufacturing_pmi.label: Manufacturing PMI
manufacturing_pmi.note: Hovering close to the 50 expansion/contraction line. New export orders remain exposed to global trade-policy uncertainty and tariff risk, a theme the ECB repeatedly flags as a downside risk to growth.

trade_policy_risks.label: Trade policy risks
trade_policy_risks.note: ECB (Economic Bulletin, Issue 4/2026, June 2026): risks to growth are skewed to the downside, mainly owing to the war in the Middle East, which has added to a volatile global policy environment. Specific channels flagged: (1) energy -- a prolonged supply interruption could push prices higher, eroding real incomes and investment; (2) shipping/supply chains -- closure of major routes (traffic continues to be rerouted via the Cape of Good Hope around Red Sea/Suez security risks) could create acute input shortages; (3) trade friction -- additional frictions in international trade could disrupt supply chains further, reducing exports and weakening consumption and investment; (4) Russia's war against Ukraine remains a further source of uncertainty. On inflation, risks are skewed to the upside: a bigger or longer-lasting energy-price rise could spill over into wages and other prices, and trade-tension-driven supply fragmentation could constrain critical raw materials. Update this note each quarter from the latest ECB Economic Bulletin (ecb.europa.eu/press/economic-bulletin).

unemployment.label: Unemployment rate
unemployment.note: Unemployment has stayed near its record low right through the post-2022 slowdown: firms held on to staff rather than shedding them, which supports household consumption but keeps wage growth — and with it services inflation — from cooling quickly, one of the reasons the ECB treats the disinflation path as data-dependent rather than settled. This card is EA21, not EA20 like the others: Eurostat publishes no monthly EA20 unemployment aggregate (Bulgaria joined the euro in January 2026).
